meta.description: Structures biological experiments so inference is valid by construction, covering Fisher's principles (randomization, replication, local control), the experimental-vs-observational unit distinction and pseudoreplication (Hurlbert 1984; Lazic 2018), randomization mechanics, blocking layouts (RCBD, Latin square, incomplete block), factorial designs and interactions, and the split-plot/nested error strata hidden inside multi-batch genomics.
meta.audit_type: first audit; not tied to a candidate Specialist
meta.executed_inputs: 5/7 (inputs 1-5 ran real R code on synthetic data; inputs 6-7 are Mode A scope/adversarial reasoning tests with no code to run)

scientific_integrity.detail: All 11 citations (Hurlbert 1984, Lazic 2018, Kenward & Roger 1997, Barr 2013, Matuschek 2017, Morgan & Rubin 2012, Pocock & Simon 1975, Auer & Doerge 2010, etc.) are real, correctly attributed papers in this literature. Every number in this audit was computed by this session on labelled synthetic data; no fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, sample sizes, or p-values.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research/animal/cell experimental-design scope only; no individual diagnostic or prescriptive claims; not patient-facing, so no medical-disclaimer requirement applies.

methodological_ground.detail: No methodological fallacy found in the Skill's content. The adversarial input (7) confirms the Skill's own guidance actively refuses the fallacy (cell-level pseudoreplication for a spurious p-value) rather than committing it.

code_usability.detail: All 5 code-bearing inputs ran to completion on lme4 2.0.6 / lmerTest 3.2.1 / dplyr 1.2.1 (installed, confirmed via r.sh) with no syntax errors, missing dependencies, or infinite loops.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness docked 1: the split-plot section's headline anti-conservative claim has no worked whole-plot-fixed-effect example (confirmed missing by Input 4). Correctness and Appropriateness both full marks, verified against 5 real runs.

reliability.note: Per the Category-2 Scene Override, strict/exact parameter handling is not penalized. Error Reporting is strong (Per-Method Failure Modes: trigger/mechanism/symptom/fix, matched by real run behavior). Fault Tolerance/Recoverability are advisory-only in this Mode A skill; no explicit 'halt on contradictory parameters' instruction.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~200 lines; usage-guide.md and examples/ cleanly separated; no context bloat.

agent_usability.note: Docked for one area needing inference (whole-plot vs sub-plot factor identification, confirmed non-trivial while building Input 4) and for feedback design being mostly implicit rather than specifying a confirmation output at each step.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language ('pseudoreplication', 'split-plot', 'what is my n'). Forgiveness scored per the Category-2 override (exact-parameter strictness is correct, not a defect); docked 1 for no explicit 'here is what I need from you' parameter checklist.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw strings, no injection surface, no data retention concerns.

maintainability.note: Clean modularity and testability (every example is seeded and independently runnable, confirmed). Docked 1: the Related Skills list is duplicated near-verbatim across SKILL.md and usage-guide.md.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger language with explicit in-scope/out-of-scope decision-tree rows, confirmed correct behavior in Input 6 (batch-design handoff); composability names 7 related skills explicitly; every example is seeded (idempotent); clear escape hatches confirmed in Inputs 6 and 7.

inputs.label: Blocking on a near-noise factor (cage) with only 2 blocks available
inputs.note: Blocked model's p-value for condition is worse than unblocked (0.491 vs 0.268), matching the documented 'blocking on noise costs power' symptom. Surfaced a real nuance: with only 2 blocks, the block-SS estimate itself is noisy (see P2 recommendation).
inputs.execution_note: run/in3_blocking_on_noise.R on SYNTHETIC data (2 cages, near-zero true cage variance, seed 2026091703); output run/in3_blocking_on_noise.out.

assertions.text: Blocking on a factor with negligible true variance is shown to cost power
Only 2 blocks spends 1 of 10 residual df, a real demonstrated cost
Skill's qualitative warning holds even though the single random draw's block SS was not itself negligible
assertions.note: correctly interpreted as sampling noise at n=2 blocks

inputs.label: Split-plot: 3 sequencing lanes (whole plot), 2 WT/2 KO per lane (sub-plot)
inputs.note: lmer(expression ~ genotype + (1|lane)) ran cleanly; lane random-effect variance estimated at 3.62 (>0); mixed-model SE for genotype (0.24) much smaller than flat lm()'s SE (1.01); Satterthwaite DenDF=8 matches skill's stated small-EU correction. Surfaced a gap: this scenario only exercises the sub-plot case, not the skill's specific whole-plot anti-conservative claim (see P1).

assertions.note: no errors, anova() and summary() both printed

assertions.text: Lane random-effect variance is estimated as clearly >0

key_strengths: Exceptionally well-cited, precise treatment of the experimental-unit/pseudoreplication distinction (Hurlbert 1984; Lazic 2018), verified correct against real seeded R code across 5 of 7 tested scenarios.

Explicit, disciplined scope boundaries: correctly defers sequencing-batch allocation to batch-design and regulated-trial randomization to clinical-biostatistics rather than overreaching (confirmed in Input 6).
Refuses to help game significance via cell-level pseudoreplication and explains the correct, likely-underpowered alternative instead (confirmed in Input 7, the adversarial test).

Per-Method Failure Modes and Common Errors tables give concrete trigger/mechanism/symptom/fix guidance that matched real code behavior in this audit (blocking-on-noise power cost, split-plot SE differences both reproduced on synthetic data).

recommendations.title: Split-plot section's headline claim has no matching worked example
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md states a flat analysis is anti-conservative for the whole-plot factor, but its only code example has just one fixed effect (sub-plot), never a fixed effect that varies between whole plots.
recommendations.root_cause: The prose describes the whole-plot risk but the single code block only demonstrates the sub-plot case.
recommendations.fix: Add a second short example with a genuine whole-plot fixed effect (e.g. incubator temperature per run) crossed with a sub-plot fixed effect, showing the flat model's anti-conservative SE for the whole-plot term next to the correct two-stratum model's larger, honest SE.

recommendations.title: No caution about block-count reliability at very small block counts
recommendations.problem: This audit's run showed that with only 2 blocks, the estimate of block variance is itself unreliable (1 df) — a real design trap the skill doesn't name.
recommendations.root_cause: The Quantitative Thresholds table covers small EU counts (df corrections) but not small block counts specifically.
recommendations.fix: Add a row noting RCBD needs a minimum block count (e.g. >=3-4) before the block-variance estimate itself can be trusted, cross-referenced from the existing 'blocking on noise' failure mode.

recommendations.title: Related Skills list duplicated near-verbatim across two files
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md each carry their own, overlapping Related Skills list.
recommendations.root_cause: No single source of truth for the cross-reference list.
recommendations.fix: Keep the list in SKILL.md only; have usage-guide.md point to it.
